title: Roadtripeado — Travel & Business Mapping
subtitle: Travel mapping, route planning and paid guides for 7,000+ users
description: A full-stack travel mapping platform serving 7,000+ real users, with interactive maps, route planning, location search and paid travel guides. My work spans the Next.js frontend and Express/TypeScript backend, alongside subscriptions, messaging and media services.
highlights: Built a travel mapping platform serving 7,000+ real users with interactive maps, route planning, location search and paid guides.
Implemented tiered Stripe subscriptions for business map visibility.
Built location listings, category filters and favourites with MongoDB.
Developed award milestones for achievements and free-map access.
Integrated Socket.io messaging with database-backed chat history.
Added S3/Sharp media uploads, Zod validation, scheduled tasks and Winston logging.
role: Full-stack development: Next.js interface, interactive maps and location search, route planning, backend APIs, Stripe subscriptions and real-time messaging.
problem: The product brings location discovery, paid business visibility and traveller engagement into one directory.

focus.title: Subscription-based business visibility
focus.body: Implemented tiered Stripe subscriptions so local businesses could list locations and offers on the map.

focus.title: Location discovery and engagement
focus.body: Built location listings, category filtering and favourites with MongoDB, alongside award milestones that unlock achievements and free maps.

focus.title: Messaging and backend operations
focus.body: Integrated Socket.io chat with stored message history, AWS S3 uploads processed with Sharp, Zod validation, scheduled tasks and Winston logging.

decisions.implementation: Listing visibility is connected to subscription plans.
decisions.reasoning: A billing provider fits recurring paid access; the application still needs to keep listing permissions aligned with each plan.
decisions.result: The platform serves 7,000+ real users with interactive travel maps, route planning and paid travel guides.

decisions.implementation: Real-time messaging is paired with stored chat history.
decisions.reasoning: Live delivery and persistence serve different needs: an open connection delivers messages, while storage keeps the conversation available later.

title: Quran International — Islamic Content Platform
subtitle: Multilingual content APIs, subscriptions and reading progress
description: An Islamic content platform with Quran, Hadith, Tafsir and a knowledge library. My backend work covered multilingual content, reading features, subscriptions, real-time communication and notifications using Express, TypeScript and MongoDB.
highlights: Built multilingual Quran, Hadith, Tafsir and knowledge-library data features.
Implemented bookmarks, highlights, last-read syncing and Hasanat tracking.
Integrated web and in-app subscription support.
Developed real-time chat, support messaging and push notifications.
Built administrative features for content, user support and subscription analytics.
role: Backend development: content APIs and storage, reading progress, Stripe and in-app subscriptions, real-time features and notifications.
problem: The application combines multilingual religious content with personal reading progress, paid access and community features.

focus.title: Multilingual content and reading features
focus.body: Built storage and data processing for Quran, Hadith, Tafsir and library content, with bookmarks, highlights, last-read syncing and Hasanat tracking.

focus.title: Web and in-app subscriptions
focus.body: Implemented subscription support for web payments through Stripe and in-app purchases.

focus.title: Communication and administration
focus.body: Integrated real-time chat, support messaging and push notifications, alongside administrative features for content, support and subscription analytics.

decisions.implementation: Bookmarks, highlights and last-read state are stored alongside content features.
decisions.reasoning: Persistent reading state supports returning readers; multilingual content and personal progress remain separate concerns.
decisions.result: Readers can save highlights, bookmark content and resume reading.

decisions.implementation: The backend supports web and in-app subscription purchases.
decisions.reasoning: Multiple payment channels need a shared application access model, even though each provider has its own purchase flow.
decisions.result: Subscription support covers web payments and in-app purchases.

title: ClipFrame — Content Scheduling & Meta Integration
subtitle: Scheduled publishing, background jobs and subscription limits
description: A social content platform for brand onboarding, content planning and Instagram/Facebook publishing. My backend work combined Express and TypeScript APIs with BullMQ/Redis background jobs, Meta integrations, Stripe subscriptions and media storage.
highlights: Built content scheduling and Facebook/Instagram business-page integrations.
Implemented asynchronous background jobs with BullMQ and Redis.
Added Stripe subscription plans with weekly content and business limits.
Supported brand onboarding, reusable templates and content planning.
Integrated media storage, real-time alerts, OAuth and documented APIs.
role: Content automation development: Next.js workflows, scheduling APIs, Facebook/Instagram Meta integration, BullMQ/Redis jobs, subscription limits and webhooks.
problem: Businesses need to manage brand assets, plan content and schedule publishing while staying within their subscription limits.

focus.title: Planning and social publishing
focus.body: Implemented content workflows for weekly planners and reusable templates, with scheduling for Instagram and Facebook and reminder triggers.

focus.title: Background processing and media
focus.body: Used BullMQ and Redis for asynchronous jobs, AWS S3 and Cloudinary for media storage, and Socket.io for real-time alerts.

focus.title: Access, limits and documentation
focus.body: Integrated Stripe plan management and weekly content limits, Passport OAuth, rate limiting and Swagger API documentation.

decisions.implementation: Asynchronous jobs support scheduled Facebook and Instagram publishing.
decisions.reasoning: A queue separates scheduled work from the request that creates it. Provider failures, retries and job timing are concerns to account for in this approach.
decisions.result: Content planning is connected to scheduled social publishing.

decisions.implementation: Stripe plans are paired with weekly content and business limits.
decisions.reasoning: Billing status and product usage are different responsibilities: the application must apply the limits associated with each plan.
decisions.result: Weekly content allowances follow subscription plans.

title: Ascela — Cycle, Nutrition & Fitness Tracking
subtitle: Wellness APIs, AI recipe features and Flutter integration
description: A wellness application combining cycle tracking, meal and workout logs, and personalised recipe features. My work focused on its Express/TypeScript backend and REST/WebSocket integration with a Flutter mobile app.
highlights: Built cycle tracking, meal logs, workout history and grocery/pantry features.
Implemented AI recipe interactions with daily usage limits.
Added Stripe subscriptions, trial eligibility and billing management.
Integrated REST/WebSocket APIs with the Flutter mobile application.
Supported administrative views for platform, subscription and revenue data.
role: Backend development and Flutter API integration: tracking features, AI recipe interactions, subscriptions, real-time APIs and notifications.
problem: The mobile application brings cycle information, nutrition, fitness records and subscription access into a shared experience.

focus.title: Tracking and recipe features
focus.body: Built cycle-phase and calendar features, meal/workout logs, grocery lists and pantry management, alongside AI recipe recommendations with save, favourite, swipe and daily usage limits.

focus.title: Subscription lifecycle
focus.body: Implemented Stripe Checkout and billing features covering plan management, trial eligibility, pause, resume, cancellation and the billing portal.

focus.title: Mobile and admin integration
focus.body: Integrated REST and WebSocket APIs with the Flutter application and supported administrative statistics, subscription analytics and revenue views.

decisions.challenge: Web services for a mobile product
decisions.implementation: Backend endpoints and real-time APIs are integrated with a Flutter application.
decisions.reasoning: Request/response APIs suit saved tracking data; a live connection supports features that need updates while the app is open.
decisions.result: The mobile app connects tracking and real-time features to backend services.

decisions.implementation: Subscriptions include trial eligibility, pause, resume, cancellation and billing portal access.
decisions.reasoning: Subscription access changes over time. The integration needs to account for lifecycle changes as well as the initial checkout.
decisions.result: Users have subscription and billing-management workflows.

title: Bean Fien — Coffee Storefront & Admin Dashboard
subtitle: Next.js commerce, loyalty rewards and backend services
description: A specialty coffee application with a customer storefront and administrative dashboard. My full-stack work covered the Next.js interface, Redux Toolkit state, Recharts reporting, and Express/TypeScript services for payments, rewards and live updates.
highlights: Built a Next.js storefront with menu navigation, cart and gift-card tools.
Developed a Recharts admin dashboard for revenue, orders and categories.
Implemented loyalty points and coupon-claiming workflows.
Built MongoDB-backed services with JWT access/refresh tokens and social login.
Integrated Stripe checkout, live updates, background jobs and media uploads.
role: Full-stack development: Next.js storefront, admin dashboard, Express/TypeScript APIs, authentication and loyalty features.
problem: The product connects customer ordering and loyalty features with the administrative views needed to manage orders and revenue.

focus.title: Customer-facing commerce
focus.body: Built a responsive Next.js storefront with menu navigation, a cart drawer and gift-card tools, connected to Stripe checkout services.

focus.title: Administrative visibility
focus.body: Developed a dashboard using Recharts for revenue, order and category views, with Socket.io live updates.

focus.title: Backend and loyalty features
focus.body: Built loyalty points and coupon workflows, MongoDB schemas and indexes, JWT access/refresh authentication, social login, BullMQ/Redis jobs and S3 uploads.

decisions.implementation: A storefront and reporting dashboard connect to backend commerce services.
decisions.reasoning: Different interfaces can serve different tasks while relying on the same underlying order, payment and loyalty data.
decisions.result: Customers have menu, cart and gift-card tools; administrators have order and revenue views.

decisions.implementation: Payment integration sits alongside loyalty points and coupon workflows.
decisions.reasoning: Payments and rewards are connected business flows, but they need distinct records and rules to keep their responsibilities clear.
decisions.result: Checkout, loyalty points and coupon claiming are supported.

title: Photopia — Media Booking & Payouts
subtitle: Stripe Connect, Next.js administration and mobile APIs
description: A media booking platform connecting backend services, a Next.js admin portal and a Flutter mobile application. My work covered backend APIs, professional payouts, administration and collaboration with the mobile team.
highlights: Implemented Stripe Connect split payments for professional payouts.
Built a Next.js admin dashboard for categories, themes and platform metrics.
Designed and documented REST APIs for web and mobile integration.
Developed Socket.io messaging and notification scheduling.
Collaborated with the Flutter team on API integration and push notifications.
role: Backend and Next.js admin development, plus REST/WebSocket API collaboration with the Flutter mobile team.
problem: The platform needs to coordinate media bookings, professional earnings, communication and administrative management across web and mobile clients.

focus.title: Professional payment flows
focus.body: Implemented Stripe Connect split-payment logic for professional earnings payouts.

focus.title: Administration and API design
focus.body: Built a Next.js admin dashboard for service categories, themes and platform metrics, and designed and documented REST APIs for client integration.

focus.title: Mobile communication
focus.body: Built Socket.io messaging and notification scheduling, and collaborated with the Flutter team on API data flows and push notifications.

decisions.implementation: Split-payment logic supports professional earnings payouts.
decisions.reasoning: Marketplace payments involve multiple recipients. A connected-account payment service fits that flow, with payout and booking records still managed by the application.
decisions.result: Professional earnings have a split-payment and payout workflow.

decisions.challenge: One backend across web and mobile
decisions.implementation: A Next.js admin portal and Flutter integration share backend APIs and messaging features.
decisions.reasoning: Documented APIs give web and mobile teams a common integration surface; real-time messaging handles live communication.
decisions.result: Administration and mobile client integration connect to the platform services.
